result.question:
The last maintenance job on Transformer 1 at site MAIN was supposed to deal with the gassing, and I want to know whether it actually worked.

Find the most recently closed work order on Transformer 1. Give me its number, description, completion date, resolution notes and failure code, and tell me which fault it was meant to fix.

Then look at the oil samples taken after that date, within 2024-01-15T00:00:00.000000 to 2024-01-19T00:00:00.000000. Use hydrogen, methane, ethane, ethylene, acetylene and co. Screen hydrogen, acetylene and co for anomalous samples with a proper anomaly detection model rather than a fixed threshold. Separately, run a dissolved gas fault classification on the latest complete sample and compare its fault class with the fault the job was meant to fix.

Decide as follows:
- If both checks point to trouble, meaning at least one anomaly is flagged and the classification still shows the same fault or a higher-energy one, call the fix ineffective. Create a priority 2 corrective follow-up work order that references the original work order number, and code it with the closest failure code from our catalog.
- If only one of the two checks points to trouble, don't create a corrective job. Recommend a confirmatory oil resample within 7 days and say which check disagreed.
- If neither points to trouble, say the fix appears to have held.

If the closed job was oil filtration, degassing or regeneration, the gas levels will have been reset. In that case, judge the result on the rate of change after the job, not on absolute levels, and say you did so.

If no work order on Transformer 1 was closed before or during the window, say so, use all samples in the window, and give only the classification and anomaly result without a verdict on any fix. If fewer than 4 samples fall after the completion date, skip the anomaly model and compare the first and last post-job values instead.
result.answer:
**Work order check:** There is **no closed work order on Transformer 1 at site MAIN** before or during the 2024-01-15 → 2024-01-19 window. The only work order on this asset is **1000051** ("OLTC inspection - Transformer 1 on-load tap changer, suspected contact wear/coking", PdM, priority 1), and it is still in **WAPPR** status with no actual start/finish, resolution notes, or failure code. Therefore there is no completion date, resolution, failure code, or "fault the job was meant to fix" to compare against, and per your instructions I give only the classification and anomaly result — **no verdict on any fix**.

**Samples used (all in window, 4 samples):** 2024-01-15 through 2024-01-18 (daily). H₂ 2845→2900 ppm, CH₄ 7406→7350, C₂H₆ 5467→5450, C₂H₄ 16684→16600, C₂H₂ 7→7, CO 32→33.

**Anomaly detection (model-based, not fixed threshold):** A SubLOF detector (sktime.detection.lof.SubLOF, window_size 4, n_neighbors 2, novelty mode) fit on the multivariate hydrogen / acetylene / CO series flagged **1 anomaly out of 4 observations — the 2024-01-16 sample** (index 1). The other three samples were not flagged. Note the run/result record: n_anomalies=1, anomaly_indices=[1], anomaly_label=[0,1,0,0].

**DGA classification (latest complete sample, 2024-01-18):** The interpret_dga tool returned "LLM unavailable" after repeated retries, so I computed the IEC 60599 Rogers ratios manually:
- r1 = C₂H₂/C₂H₄ = 7/16600 ≈ 0.0004 → code 0
- r2 = CH₄/H₂ = 7350/2900 ≈ 2.53 → code 2
- r3 = C₂H₄/C₂H₆ = 16600/5450 ≈ 3.05 → code 3 (borderline 2/3)

Code combination **0-2-2/3** → **thermal fault, high temperature (T2/T3, roughly 300–700 °C)**, driven by dominant ethylene with negligible acetylene — a hot metal / thermal condition, not arcing.

**Summary:** One anomalous sample (2024-01-16) was flagged by the anomaly model, and the latest complete sample classifies as a high-temperature thermal fault. Since no work order on Transformer 1 was closed before or during the window, I'm making **no verdict on whether any fix held** — this is the classification and anomaly result only, as you specified.

task_choices: omitted / anything else  - FORECASTING: transforms -> single|ensemble -> conformal
tsfm_anomaly_detection   - detector path, producing dense anomaly labels
estimator_spec: model_id     - a catalog card, e.g. {"model_id": "ttm_r1_512_96"}; its sktime_class and params are read from the card (see find_models / resolve_model)
sktime_class - an inline class path + params, e.g. {"sktime_class": "sktime.forecasting.naive.NaiveForecaster", "params": {"strategy": "drift"}}
optional_blocks: transforms - list of transform specs applied to the target before the forecaster
ensemble   - {"members": [<estimator spec>, ...], "combine": "mean|median|min|max|weighted|stack", "weights": [...]} - use INSTEAD of estimator
finetune   - training block; see param_hints (lr, epochs, batch_size, ...)
save_to    - directory path; after a fine-tune, persist the fitted weights there and return checkpoint_path in the result (feed it to register_finetuned)
eval       - {"metrics": ["smape", ...]} - the first metric scores the backtest
rules: a recipe MUST carry an `estimator` or an `ensemble` (not both)
`model_id` must exist in the catalog; run_recipe errors if it does not
run_tabular_recipe extracts FLOps features first, then fits `estimator`; omit label_column for clustering
the series itself is never in the recipe - it arrives via dataset_path
